doc.title: Darius Brubeck interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 29, 2024

title: Opening chat: living in Rye after Camden Town
summary: Darius is in a studio with brother Chris; he and Catherine moved from Camden Town to Rye, drawn by Henry James.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive and I’m very pleased to have Darius Brubeck with me this morning. And you are aware, you said you’re in a studio with your brother?
Yeah, my brother Chris. In Danbury, Connecticut.
I was wondering if you and Catherine were living out of a suitcase.

We are, for the time being. We actually live in Rye, which is southeast of London about two and a bit hours away, after living in London for ten years right in the middle of it in Camden Town, which is legendary within the music community. Camden Town, that area. You know where Camden Market is?

A supergraphic of Amy Winehouse on one of the industrial building walls, we lived right above the canal. And in Camden Town every night is party night so after ten years of that and setting up my group and professional network to the level it needed to be, we decided to live like grown-ups and move out of London. And we moved down to Rye, R-Y-E, because, in a way because that’s where Henry James lived.
No kidding. What an attraction. Yeah.

Yeah. And we went there as tourists to see his house, which is a national trust property, and we thought you know Henry James did the same thing. He had a flop on the West End. As many of his novels as have been turned into films, he was, you know they’re well plotted and there are great characters, and this has nothing to do with jazz, I’m sorry.
He was a flop as a playwright and he decided well what the hell, I don’t need to be in London to write books, that’s what I’m good at, and he moved down to Rye.
And then he became more productive I would imagine.
